title: IAM startup Features: dual-path gating (explicit config vs OpenFeature)
answers: How do I add a new gated IAM API?
Why is my IAM API still flag-gated even though I set an explicit startup config?
How does the IAM builder decide between OpenFeature and explicit feature config?
body: Any IAM API gate in the builder must go through IdentityAccessManagementAPIBuilder.featureEnabled(ctx, flagKey, func(Features) bool), which uses the explicit b.features snapshot when set and falls back to b.ofClient OpenFeature evaluation otherwise. Adding a new gated IAM API requires updating all of: the API const + supportedAPIs list, the Features struct field, Features.SetAPIs, featureForAPI's switch (used by EnabledAPIs), and a new featureEnabled call site in InstallSchema/UpdateAPIGroupInfo/GetAPIRoutes. Missing any of these means the explicit-config path silently ignores the new API and it stays OpenFeature-only.
applies: pkg/registry/apis/iam register.go and features.go when adding/gating a new IAM API
says: How do I add a new feature that's startup-configurable?

Adding a new gated IAM API requires updates to: API const and supportedAPIs list, Features struct field, Features.SetAPIs, featureForAPI switch (used by EnabledAPIs), and featureEnabled call sites in InstallSchema/UpdateAPIGroupInfo/GetAPIRoutes. Missing any update means the explicit-config path silently ignores the new API and it remains OpenFeature-only, with no error signaling the misconfiguration.
